content.text: In Kenya, digital creators face a critical infrastructure gap: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators-works-how-2|payment]] processors like Stripe and PayPal are either unavailable or unreliable. This isn’t a temporary glitch—it’s a systemic barrier. For creators [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-presets-without-stripe-what-nobody-tells-you-7|COREMERCH guide to selling]] ebooks, courses, or templates, the inability to collect international payments means lost revenue and stalled growth. The solution isn’t a workaround; it’s a sovereign commerce stack built on blockchain-based payments and decentralized infrastructure. Kenyan creators are already deploying these systems, leveraging tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments to bypass geographic restrictions. This isn’t about adapting to limitations—it’s about choosing better [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-cloudflare-workers-crypto-payment-webhooks-4|The Real]]. Before you deploy, understand the seven critical elements Kenyan creators rely on to get paid internationally, without Stripe or PayPal.

content.text: The Full List With Context

Kenyan creators use these seven elements to build sovereign commerce stacks: 1. **Blockchain-based payments** via NOWPayments for 300+ cryptocurrencies with a 0.5% fee. 2. **Decentralized hosting** with GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for zero-cost, globally accessible storefronts. 3. **Backend logic** handled by Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for automated order processing. 4. **Order storage** in Supabase or Google Sheets for lightweight, scalable databases. 5. **File delivery** via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for instant, secure product downloads. 6. **Email deliverability** configured with SPF/DKIM/DMARC to ensure payment receipts aren’t flagged as spam. 7. **End-to-end testing** to verify every transaction from payment to delivery. These components work together to create a stack that’s entirely owned by the creator, with no reliance on third-party platforms.
Why Each Item on This List Matters

Blockchain-based payments remove geographic restrictions, allowing Kenyan creators to accept payments from anywhere. Decentralized hosting ensures the storefront is always accessible, even in regions with unreliable internet. Backend logic automates processes like order confirmation and file delivery, reducing manual work. Order storage in Supabase or Google Sheets keeps data lightweight and scalable. File delivery via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 ensures products are delivered instantly and securely. Email deliverability prevents payment receipts from landing in spam folders, maintaining trust with buyers. End-to-end testing ensures the entire stack functions flawlessly, from payment to product delivery. Together, these elements form a robust, sovereign infrastructure that Kenyan creators control entirely.
The Ones Most Creators Get Wrong

Most creators overlook **email deliverability**, assuming payment receipts will always reach buyers. Without SPF/DKIM/DMARC, emails often land in spam folders, damaging trust. Another common mistake is **skipping end-to-end testing**, leading to broken payment flows or failed product deliveries. Some creators also **underestimate the importance of decentralized hosting**, relying on platforms that can restrict access or shut down without warning. Finally, **choosing the wrong blockchain network** can result in high transaction fees, eroding profits. Kenyan creators prioritize low-fee networks like BSC, Solana, and TRON, ensuring transactions cost under $0.10.
Blockchain-based payments remove geographic restrictions entirely.
How to Prioritise What to Implement First

Start with **blockchain-based payments**—without this, nothing else matters. Use NOWPayments to accept cryptocurrencies with a 0.5% fee. Next, deploy **decentralized hosting** with GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages to ensure your storefront is globally accessible. Then, implement **backend logic** using Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script to automate order processing. Follow this with **order storage** in Supabase or Google Sheets to track transactions. Finally, set up **file delivery** via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 and configure **email deliverability** with SPF/DKIM/DMARC. End-to-end testing should be the last step, ensuring all components work seamlessly together.
Putting the List Into a Deployable Stack

To deploy a sovereign commerce stack, start by purchasing the **Complete Builder Kit ($197)** from https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. This kit includes all blueprints and templates needed to build your stack. Follow the step-by-step guides to set up NOWPayments for blockchain-based payments, deploy your storefront on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and configure backend logic with Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. Use Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. Configure SPF/DKIM/DMARC for email deliverability and test the entire stack end-to-end. Once deployed, you’ll own the entire infrastructure, with no reliance on third-party platforms.

Frequently Asked Questions
Why can’t Kenyan creators use Stripe or PayPal?
Stripe and PayPal are either unavailable or unreliable in Kenya due to geographic restrictions and financial regulations. Creators need sovereign infrastructure to bypass these barriers.
